Ava (DevEx): Morning quick async standup — did: updated Python SDK quickstart to use async client + added a note about prefix-KV caching in docs. Blocker: samplekit sampleapp fails CI on mac M1 runners with a segfault when building the C-extension wheel. Today: will open PR for the docs changes and try to reproduce the CI failure locally.

Samir: Ugh yeah I saw that failure last night on a test run. Do you have the failing snippet/stack?

Ava (DevEx): Here's the failing bit from CI logs:
```
RuntimeError: could not load extension 'fast_tok'
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
#0 0x7fff... in vm
```
Link: https://ci.internal/redwood/job/234/build/7 (CI artifact)

eng-runtime-bot: [ci] Build 234 failed on macos-m1 - see artifacts: /artifacts/build-234/trace.log

Priya: I can take a look on a local M1 VM after lunch. @Samir can you share the wheel build command you ran? Also agree we should gate the doc merge until we confirm the wheel is stable on arm.

Samir: build command was: `python -m build && pip wheel --no-deps --wheel-dir dist .` I suspect it's the compiled tokenizer. Repro steps: use homebrew clang + macOS SDK, then `pip install dist/fast_tok-*.whl` — segfault shows on import.

Jordan: Pinged @eng-runtime (channel) — maybe kernel selection or recent compiler flags introduced an ABI issue. If Priya finds a quick workaround we can ship docs with a note: "intel-only wheel; arm64 builds coming" :thumbsup:

Ava (DevEx): Thanks — I'll hold the docs PR until we confirm or add the note. If Priya needs a hand reproing, I can share a devkit access. Also I'll add a short changelog line about the async client API change.

Priya: Sounds good. I'll update this thread with findings by EOD.

Samir: thx — will stand by to test any temporary wheel builds.

Jordan: cc @ops for M1 runners capacity if you need longer debug runs.

Ava (DevEx): /end
